## Headline read — the most replicable thing

Will runs a multi-touch, document-driven sales motion where he owns the technical and commercial detail end-to-end. He doesn't chase; he sequences deliberately across email, call, and structured deliverables (sampling plans, contracts, carbon projections), treating each follow-up as a reason to add substance, not just bump the thread. His close is built on removing ambiguity—exact title references, completed drafts, scheduled farm visits—not persuasion.

## Conversation openers

### cold outbound (via other rep, but pattern visible in Will's follow-up touch)

**Pattern.** Regional soil-science premise + proof point from similar geography. Leads with scarcity framing (soil type as competitive advantage) and track record (ACCUs issued, hectares registered). No pitch; invites exploration.

**Verbatim:**
> "Soil types within the Riverina including Red-brown earths, Chromosols, Sodosols and transitional clay create a natural 'carbon sink' where organic matter filters into clay aggregates and locks in for 20-50 years."
> "Our Riverina Track Record: 31 registered AgriProve soil carbon projects across the region. Equating to 8,800 total hectares. 13,055 ACCUs issued to Riverina farmers to date worth over half a million dollars. We've issued more ACCUs in the Riverina than any other soil carbon developer."

### inbound / warm handoff (Justin Costello, Dan Burnham threads)

**Pattern.** Accepts inbound, moves fast to structured conversation (meeting request with agenda) rather than exploratory call. Call transcript notes show Will gathering customer intel on service experience and platform feedback.

**Verbatim:**
> "Dylan invited Justin to flag any issues to improve the experience. [from call transcript note on 2026-04-20]"
> "The aim of this meeting with Will is to clarify the final key concerns and specific questions regarding your Key Commercial Terms with the intention finalizing the document and moving forward to registering a soil carbon project with AgriProve. [farm visit agenda, Dan Burnham]"

## Discovery questions

- **Qualification via constraint removal. Will asks backward-chaining questions: what prevents execution, accessibility, approval? Not 'are you interested' but 'can we actually do this'?** — _surfaces:_ Removes operational friction before project starts. Identifies where land geometry, infrastructure, or access will kill execution. Shows Will is solving for *delivery*, not closing a sale.
  > "Are all project areas included? Are any areas included where the new activity will not be carried out? Are all obstacles such as buildings, dams, large trees, roads, steep slopes or other features that would prevent the new activity or soil sampling, excluded from the project areas? Are all sample points accessible by a vehicle? Soil sampling will be attempted to >1m. Are there any obstacles such as rocks or assets such as power, phone, gas, water or irrigation lines, which may affect sampling? [Draft Sampling Plan email to Justin Costello, 2024-03-28]"
- **Value quantification (via proxy): asks customer to compare against peer outcomes, not just abstract ACCU value.** — _surfaces:_ Customer wants specificity on return, not concept. Will responds with peer example (Ben Cassidy, 8.03 ACCUs/ha/year, 1,000 hectares) rather than generic ACCU pricing. Anchors expectation to real farm outcome.
  > "8 ACCUs per ha is impressive for soils. What is their value? [Jonathan Harpley response, 2025-12-12]"

## Transitions

### From cold email sequence (multiple touches, proof points) → call + structured meeting

After 3–4 emails (regional insight, track record, peer case study, free tool offer), Will or team pivot to phone + calendar. Call is inbound or outbound, but meeting invite includes explicit agenda (e.g., 'clarify final key concerns regarding Key Commercial Terms').

> "[2025-12-05 to 2025-12-12: 4 emails, then] [2026-04-15: inbound call from Jonathan Harpley, then outbound call, then] [2026-04-20: structured meeting scheduled 'Post Carbon Project Plan and Key Commercial Terms Call']"
> "[2024-05-29 call with Dan Burnham, then] [2024-05-29 email invite to webinar], [later] [2026-02-24 farm visit meeting with explicit agenda on Key Commercial Terms]"

### From discovery call / webinar attendance / warm interest signal → site visit + document review

Doesn't loop back to email nurture. Escalates immediately to farm visit with ops leadership (Head of Operations Will Frecheville noted in Dan Burnham thread) and sends draft agreements in advance so visit focuses on removing objections, not explaining product.

> "AgriProve - Farm Visit with Head of Operations - Will Frecheville, Dan Burnham and Emma-Jane Burnham- Tuesday the 24th of Feb at 4:30pm (QLD Time). The aim of this meeting with Will is to clarify the final key concerns and specific questions regarding your Key Commercial Terms with the intention finalizing the document and moving forward to registering a soil carbon project with AgriProve."

### From information request (title, CEA boundaries, sampling logistics) → revised contract / amended deed

When customer flags a doc issue (missing title, CEA boundary, non-CEA areas), Will turns around corrected version within same thread, often same day. Shows attention to detail; removes friction for next step (customer sign-off).

> "[2024-12-03 Deane: 'Please review and advise the missing title and update both documents (ERF Participation Deed and Novation Deed Annexe 2)'] [2024-12-04 Will: 'My apologies – that was an omission on my part. Please see updated Novation and Variation inclusive of the correct titles: Lots 1 and 2 on TP107252; and Lot 1 on TP319975. We did not have this last week. Hope this clarifies it for you.']"

Lead status: Disqualified. Yet inbound calls 2026-02-18 onward suggest re-engagement; new criteria may have shifted (cousin's CarbonLink credits approved, or land changed). ## Customer archetypes — who they engaged well

### Long-cycle, multi-stakeholder landholder (owner + spouse, or co-operators)

**Characteristics.** 400+ hectares, established farming operation, grazing or mixed cropping, likely in Riverina/QLD, already thinking about land management (stocking rates, pasture seeding, avoiding clearing). Cautious on new schemes; wants peer validation and clear commercial terms before commitment.

**Approach.** Multi-touch proof (regional soil science + track record + named peer farm outcome), then site visit with ops leadership (Head of Operations) to address 'final key concerns.' Documents prepared in advance. Removes friction by arriving with drafts, not questions.

**Example.** Dan Burnham (Burnham Grazing, grazing operation, Central Queensland): 2024-05-29 discovery call → webinar nurture → 2026-02-24 farm visit with Head of Operations Will Frecheville + ops. Multiple calls pre- and post-visit. Deal moving toward Key Commercial Terms finalization.

### Growth-minded regional farmer, active on industry networks

**Characteristics.** Farms 400–1,500 hectares, engaged with industry bodies (CFA, soil carbon networks), owns the land, curious about new revenue streams, checks peer performance and ACCU value before deciding.

**Approach.** Hyperlocal soil science credential + peer case study (same region, same soil type, same farm size), then free tool trial to model own farm. Fast move to phone once prospect engages (inbound calls = high intent). Structured project planning call when ready.

**Example.** Jonathan Harpley (Growth Farms, Riverina): 2025-12-05 through 2025-12-12 emails (soil science → track record → Ben Cassidy case study) → 2026-04-15 inbound calls (multiple) → 2026-04-20 structured 'Post Carbon Project Plan and Key Commercial Terms Call.' Deal moving forward.

### Operator / broker (B2B: carbon project manager, farm manager, land partnership)

**Characteristics.** Responsible for multiple projects or landholders, coordinates with AgriProve ops team, manages contracts, titles, CEA boundaries. Less decision fatigue (farming is known), more process focus (correctness, timing, regulatory alignment).

**Approach.** Document-driven, detail-oriented. Will responds to doc requests with precision (corrected titles, updated deeds, Variation Declarations) same-day. Regular ops sync meetings (weekly or bi-weekly). Treats ops contact as peer, not lead.

**Example.** Harrison Clark (LawrieCo, Projects and Carbon Development Manager): 2022-12-19 onwards, weekly 'Op's coordination LawrieCo / AgriProve' meetings (at least 5+). 2024-06-10 through 2024-06-25 email coordination on Lawrence, Bolkus, Sinclair projects (titles, RFI responses, eligible activities). 2025-06-18 outbound call (routine check-in).

### Legacy / service customer (post-registration monitoring and support)

**Characteristics.** Already registered with AgriProve, now in project delivery / monitoring phase. Provides feedback on platform, website changes, Horizon platform status. Relationship maintenance is key; customer success owns most of the contact.

**Approach.** Regular customer success calls (not sales calls). Invite to flag service issues. Long relationship threads (2+ years, multiple touchpoints). Will is secondary to customer success team; call notes show Will listening for product feedback, not selling.

**Example.** Justin Costello (customer, 74 engagements): 2023-12-19 initial meeting → 2024-03-28 to 2024-04-04 sampling plan review → 2025-10-21 onwards, inbound and outbound calls (service touch). 2026-04-20 call transcript: 'Justin teasing Dylan about retirement leave, then catching up on project status. Long substantive customer call. Discussed website changes, Horizon platform status.' Classification: Customer Success folder.

## Anti-patterns visible

- **Minimal direct objection rebuttal; when objections are raised (e.g., 'may not be much benefit to start a carbon project'), Will's team opts to disqualify rather than overcome. No evidence of 'here's why you should reconsider' responses.** — Dan Burnham: 2024-05-29 note concludes 'Lead Status Update: Not a Landholder = Not a lead. Not interested = Disqualified.' Then 2026-02 inbound calls arrive and are handled, but no sales reactivation email or 'let's revisit' outreach. Suggests Will assumes objections are terminal unless customer re-engages.
- **Long dormancy between engagement phases. Justin Costello: 2024-04-04 sampling plan bump → then no email engagement visible until 2025-10-21 inbound call (18 months later). Jonathan Harpley: 2025-12-12 last email → 2026-04-15 inbound call (4 months later, but customer-initiated). Pattern suggests nurture sequence may not be automated or rigorous once deal enters 'waiting for customer' phase.** — Justin Costello (74 engagements) shows 4 emails over 1 week (Mar 28 – Apr 4), then silence until Oct 2025. Jonathan Harpley (62 engagements) shows 4 emails over 7 days (Dec 5–12), then 4 months of silence before inbound calls. Email frequency drops precipitously post-discovery; no cadence visible for re-engagement or milestone updates.
- **Limited visibility on deal size, ACCU price negotiation, or contract variance. All examples show Will accepting customer/ops requirements (title corrections, area exclusions, eligible activity adjustments) without visible push-back or commercial negotiation. Suggests either (a) margins are wide, (b) deals are standardized, or (c) commercial negotiation is handled by a different role.** — Deane (RAF): 'Please review and advise the missing title... update both documents.' Will: corrects and sends same-day, no conditional push-back. Harrison Clark (LawrieCo): RFI responses from regulator, Will confirms 'I'm satisfied that we could implement all of these,' but no mention of fee adjustment or timeline trade-off.
